name: nav-menu
description:
The full-screen menu a narrow `navbar` opens.

It was a centred column of large words on a tinted wash — the default full-screen menu that every site has, and nothing about it belonged to this brand. Rebuilt out of the devices the rest of the system already uses: an eyebrow naming the band, a left-aligned column with a real reading edge, a hairline rhythm between items, a marker bar on the current one, and a meta line saying what each destination IS. A menu of five words tells you their names; a menu with a line under each tells you which one you want.

LEFT-ALIGNED, and that is the biggest change. Centred display type is the generic answer, and it is also the harder one to read: five centred lines have five different starting points, so the eye re-finds the left edge on every row. Every other index in this system — the sidebar, the navbar, the footer — reads down a single edge, and this one now does too.

A SEPARATE composite from `navbar`, for a structural reason rather than tidiness. The bar is `backdrop-filter` glass, and a filtered element creates a containing block for `position: fixed` descendants — so a menu nested inside the bar is trapped in the bar's box and covers nothing. The real header found this and renders the menu as a SIBLING. Any implementation that nests this will look correct in a harness and fail on the page.

base.$description:
`position: fixed` over the whole viewport at the overlay layer — BELOW the bar, deliberately, so the bar's own control stays reachable and the menu cannot cover the thing that dismisses it.

A container like every other composite: `inset: 0` gives it a width from outside its contents, and the type below sizes in `cqi` so the menu is right at any size it is given rather than only at full screen.

scrim.$description: Marine, and nearly solid. It was 90% with a heavy blur — a frosted sheet, which is a device this brand uses for the NAVBAR and should not repeat here: two glass layers in one interaction and neither reads as the front one. 97% with a light blur is a ground, and the page behind stays faintly present so dismissing feels like closing rather than navigating back.

close.$description:
A WAY OUT, in the corner. The menu had none — it relied on the bar's toggle showing through from above, which works only while the bar is rendered over the overlay and is invisible to anyone who does not already know. A full-screen takeover with no visible dismiss is the most common trap-the-user bug there is, and Escape does not help a touch user.

Outlined in the ink at 25%, never filled — the treatment `voice-pill` gives its side controls, because a filled button here would compete with the destinations.

panel.$description: A reading column, not a centred splash. `max-inline-size` plus `margin-inline: auto` gives the menu a real left edge at any width — the thing every other index in this system has and this one did not.

crest.$description: The mark. Every full-surface moment in this system leads with it — `flow-card` made `crest` a slot for exactly this reason: a takeover with no identity on it is a page you reconstruct from its links.

eyebrow.$description: Composes `text text--eyebrow`, inverted. The brand's signature device — it names the band the eye is about to read — and the menu was the one full-surface moment without one. Only the colour is this unit's.

items.$description: A list with a rhythm, not a stack of words. Each row has a hairline above it, which is what turns five destinations into a scannable index — the same decision `sidebar` makes at a quarter of the size.

item.$description:
One destination. `clamp(1.75rem, 7cqi, 3rem)` in the display face — `cqi`, the container's inline size, not `vw`: the real header uses `11vw` and is right by coincidence, because there the menu happens to BE the viewport. Measured against its own container it is right everywhere.

The whole row is the target, and the row is padded rather than the text — a 3rem word with a 3rem hit area is a link you can miss above and below.
item.transition: background var(--duration-quick) var(--ease-out), padding-inline-start var(--duration-quick) var(--ease-out)

meta.$description: What the destination IS, under its name. A menu of five words tells you their names; a line under each tells you which one you want — and it is the difference between a splash screen and a table of contents.

marker.$description: The bar beside the current destination — the same device `sidebar` uses, at this surface's scale. Present on every row at `opacity: 0` and revealed by the selected state, so the current item settles rather than the bar appearing from nothing.

footer.$description: What sits under the destinations — the language switch, and a line saying who you are talking to. Separated by a rule rather than a gap: it is not the last item in the list, it is what the list sits above.

trust.$description: One quiet line. A page that ends on purpose rather than simply stopping — the composition rule this surface was missing.

tone.$description: The ground the menu lays over.

solid.$description: No blur — for a surface where the page behind is noise rather than context, and for the browsers that cannot do it.

hover.$description: The row tints and steps in. Moving the text rather than only colouring it is what makes a 3rem target feel like a control — at this size a colour change alone is easy to miss because the glyphs are mostly negative space.

selected.$description: The page you are already on: accent ink, and the marker bar revealed. The accent is the one colour on a marine ground that is neither the foreground nor a dimmed version of it — but colour alone is what people miss on a dim screen, so the bar carries it too.

reducedMotion.$description: It still opens and every destination is still there; only the movement goes. Removing the ANIMATION without this would leave the panel at `opacity: 0` — the classic reduced-motion bug, where the transition was the only thing revealing the content.

a11y.note:
A visible CLOSE control, not only Escape — a full-screen takeover with no visible dismiss traps anyone who did not know the keyboard shortcut, and Escape is no help on a touch screen.

A dialog in everything but name: while it is open, focus is trapped inside it, Escape closes it, and focus returns to the toggle that opened it. The page behind is `inert` — without that a screen reader and a Tab key both walk straight through the scrim into a page the sighted user cannot see.

ONE navigation landmark, not two. The menu holds the same links the bar does, so it must be the same `<nav>` moved rather than a hidden second copy; two landmarks with one label is a screen reader announcing the navigation twice.

The current destination carries `aria-current="page"` and is marked by accent ink AND a bar, never by colour alone.

`visibility: hidden` rather than `display: none` in the closed state, so the open transition has something to animate from — and so the closed menu is genuinely out of the tab order, which `opacity: 0` alone does not do.
